captions.text: Kennedy Space Center, in Florida. A rocket roars into the night.
It carries supplies to the space station, high above Earth.
Inside, something is growing in a strange pink glow...
First, tiny sprouts. And not one ray of sunshine.
Bright lamps shine all day. Four weeks later, the lettuce is ready to eat!
Back in Florida, scientists test one light at a time.
So does light really matter? Let's find out.

Something around a living thing, like light, water, or temperature, that affects how it grows.
How fast something grows over a period of time. For plants, we can measure it in centimeters per day.

parts.title: Why Plants Need Light
parts.html:
Plants make their own food using sunlight. This is called photosynthesis. Without enough light, a plant can't make the energy it needs to grow tall and strong.

When a plant gets plenty of light, it grows faster. When light is weak or blocked, growth slows down, sometimes a lot.

parts.title: A Fair Test Changes One Thing
parts.html:
In a fair test, scientists change only one thing at a time. In this investigation, the only difference between the two plants is light. The soil, the water, and the pot all stay the same.

That way, if the plants grow differently, we know light is the reason. The one thing we change on purpose is called the variable.

parts.title: Reading the Data
parts.html:
Scientists measure plant height in centimeters and write it in a data table. Then they build a graph, so the pattern is easy to see.

Light changes things in nature, too. Sunlight gets dimmer as it goes down through water. Let's ride down and find out where plants can still grow.

compare.frame: This plant ___, so it grew in ___.

curator.A: Green and sturdy → bright light. Light lets a plant make its own food. With plenty of food, it grows wide green leaves and a strong stem.
curator.B: Pale and stretched → the dark. With no light, the sprouts can't make food. They stretch up fast, reaching for light, using food stored in the seed. But they stay pale and weak.

after.kicker: 🎬 Behind the scenes · Taller isn't always healthier
after.alt: A tall, thin plant with yellow leaves and a purple stem, growing in a crate in a dark basement
after.html: This plant grew in a dark basement. It stretched up tall, reaching for light. But its leaves are yellow and its stem is thin and weak. A plant in the dark can grow tall for a while, using food stored in its seed. When that food runs out, it stops growing. Taller isn't always healthier!

wall.title: How deep can plants grow?
wall.look: A cutaway (a slice) of the water, from a sunny Florida spring down to the deep sea. It is a model. Each level is deeper and darker than the one above it. The brass dial on the left shows which level you are at.
wall.do: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing layer: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the plant shows.

predict.q: How deep do you think plants can grow?
options: all the way to the bottom
All the way to the bottom of the sea
predict.mine: Your prediction: {p}. Let's ride down and find out.
predict.confirm: You predicted plants grow only where sunlight reaches. The evidence agrees: deep down, where light can't reach, there are no plants.
predict.change: You predicted plants grow all the way down. The evidence changed that idea: on the dark deep-sea floor, there are no plants at all.

wall.skyAlt: A clear spring surrounded by green trees under a blue sky with white clouds
wall.locked: Brush the level above first. The elevator goes down, one level at a time.
wall.first: Brush the glowing top layer. Drag across it (or tap it again and again).
wall.endText: Look at the line. Near the top, where sunlight is bright, plants grow tall and thick. As the water gets deeper and darker, there are fewer plants. In the deep sea, there are none.
wall.rule: Plants grow only where enough light reaches them. Less light means less food, so fewer plants can grow. With no light, plants can't grow at all.
choices: 🌤️ Still light: a wide green meadow
🌥️ Dim light: low algae on rock
🌑 No light: no plants at all

wow.title: A garden with 180 lamps
wow.alt: Rows of green wheat plants growing inside a metal chamber full of tubes and wires
wow.caption: Wheat growing in NASA's Advanced Plant Habitat, a plant chamber on the space station.
wow.html:
There's no sunshine inside the space station, so NASA built plant chambers full of lamps. One of them, the Advanced Plant Habitat, has about 180 small lamps that scientists can change from Earth.

They turn some colors up and others down, one change at a time, to see which light helps plants grow best. It's a fair test, in space!
wow.insetCap: Zinnia plants growing on the space station. Astronauts later saw them bloom.

keyIdea: Light is a growing condition for plants. The more light a plant gets, the more food it can make, and the faster it grows. Comparing plants with only one difference gives us evidence.

quiz.q: What does a scientist call the information collected during an investigation?

options.miss: Think about the Word Wall card for information collected in an investigation: measurements and observations.

options.ok: 🌱 That's right! Data is the information scientists collect: measurements, observations, and numbers from an investigation.

options.miss: Think about the Word Wall card for information collected in an investigation: measurements and observations.

quiz.q: In this investigation, both plants started at 2 cm but grew differently. What does that tell us?

options.t: The light condition affected how fast each plant grew.
options.ok: 🌿 Exactly! Since everything except light was the same, any difference in growth must have been caused by the light condition.

options.t: The soil must have been different in each pot.
options.miss: Remember: in this fair test, only the light was changed. So any growth difference is evidence about light, not soil or the type of plant.

options.t: The plants were different kinds of plants to begin with.
options.miss: Remember: in this fair test, only the light was changed. So any growth difference is evidence about light, not soil or the type of plant.

options.t: It lets you water the plants automatically.
options.miss: Think about what a graph does with numbers. It turns data into a picture that makes patterns easier to see and compare.

options.t: It shows you which plant is taller in real life.
options.miss: Think about what a graph does with numbers. It turns data into a picture that makes patterns easier to see and compare.

options.t: It makes patterns in the data easier to see.
options.ok: 🌱 Yes! A graph turns rows of numbers into a picture, so you can spot patterns, like which plant grew faster, at a glance.
